summary: Design and provision cross-cloud identity proxy for bastionless privileged debugging
description:
Issue summary: Oncall and SREs frequently need short-lived privileged access to customer-private deployments (VPC/private Dedicated clusters) and cross-cloud debug hosts. Current approach requires provisioning ephemeral bastions, manual cross-account role grants, or long-lived service account keys. This ticket is to design and provision a cross-cloud identity proxy pattern (AWS -> GCP/Workload Identity Federation or inverse) so engineers can obtain timebound, auditable impersonation of target service identities without creating long-lived credentials or bespoke jump hosts.

Impact: Improves mean time to resolution for incidents affecting Private/Dedicated customers, reduces blast radius of permanent permissions, and centralizes auditing. Pilot scope should reduce oncall friction and speed incident resolution by removing manual access requests.

Background: Recent incident on 2026-02-26 required multi-hour access provisioning across AWS debugging instances and GCP customer VPCs. The workaround introduced elevated long-lived bindings that needed manual revocation. We need a repeatable, auditable, least-privilege pattern for cross-cloud impersonation.

Request: Design the identity proxy service, document required IAM bindings, create terraform modules for provisioning, and implement a short-lived credential issuance flow integrated with our SSO and Vault. Provide a runbook for oncall usage and an audit trail in Cloud Logging/Cloud Audit or CloudTrail.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) SRE attempts to debug private customer cluster from AWS debug bastion.
2) SRE cannot access GCP project service account/secret because no cross-account impersonation is configured.
3) Support opens manual access request; security approves, ops creates temporary binding; incident resolution delayed.
4) Verify this flow by attempting to replicate on a staging private deployment (staging projects).
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Aisha: Collected logs from 2026-02-26 incident; repeated friction points are approval latency and key distribution.
2026-03-10 11:00 - Marco: Proof-of-concept ran using AWS STS + GCP workload identity federation; basic flow works but needs automated ephemeral binding and audit recording.
2026-03-11 14:45 - Security (J. Huang): Must ensure any auto-binding expires and all actions recorded in Cloud Audit/CloudTrail. No permanent IAM grants allowed for pilot.

Notes: Consider using Vault as a broker: AWS -> Vault exchange -> issue GCP impersonation token OR use short-lived workload-identity pools with limited token lifetime. Evaluate both for operational complexity and auditability.
comments: Aisha Patel (2026-03-10): Filing this as follow-up to recent incident. Goal is to eliminate manual cross-account RBAC edits during incidents.
Marco Alvarez (2026-03-10): I'll prototype a broker using vault-aws plugin and GCP IAMCredentials API. Will post a PoC PR and terraform snippets.

Jian Huang - Security (2026-03-11): Security approves pilot if we ship token TTL <= 1h, require SSO approval flow for escalation, and include immutable audit logs. Also require automated orphaned-binding cleanup job.
Rosa Martinez - Oncall (2026-03-12): Please include a CLI helper to request and attach ephemeral creds to a debug session; currently copying JSON keys is error prone.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc describing architecture (proxy vs vault broker) and chosen tradeoffs published to Confluence.
Terraform module that can provision workload identity pool (GCP) and trust relationship (AWS) for a pilot project.
PoC service or vault role that issues GCP impersonation tokens with TTL <= 1 hour and records issuance event to Cloud Audit/CloudTrail.
Runbook for oncall including steps, CLI helper, and emergency rollback (revoke bindings) procedure.
Security review completed and pilot signed off by Security and SRE leads.
resolution: In progress: PoC repo created and initial terraform in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2023. Next steps: finish terraform automation, integrate with Vault and SSO, and run security review. Planned pilot in us-east1 staging by 2026-03-20.
